text: VitaLife Insurance Corporation | 2025 Edition

Nomination is one of the most critical steps in life insurance. A valid, up-to-date nomination ensures that your death benefit reaches your intended beneficiary quickly, without legal complications or delays. Without a valid nomination, the claim proceeds may be subject to probate proceedings, delays, or distribution disputes among legal heirs - causing significant hardship to your family at an already difficult time.
VitaLife strongly recommends reviewing your nomination at every major life event: marriage, birth of a child, divorce, or death of a nominee.

A BENEFICIAL NOMINEE has an absolute, irrevocable right to the policy proceeds upon the death of the life assured. Creditors, legal heirs, or courts cannot attach or redirect the claim payment.

WHO QUALIFIES AS A BENEFICIAL NOMINEE: Only the following relationships qualify: - Spouse of the life assured Children of the life assured (biological or legally adopted) - Parents of the life assured - Any combination of the above

KEY  RULE:  If  you  name  your  spouse,  child,  or  parent  as  the  nominee,  they  automatically  become  a  Beneficial Nominee. You do NOT need to explicitly mark them as 'beneficial' - the relationship itself confers this status.

IMPACT ON POLICYHOLDER RIGHTS: Once a beneficial nominee is named, the policyholder CANNOT surrender, assign, or take a loan against the policy WITHOUT the written consent of the beneficial nominee (if major) or appointee (if minor). This is a significant constraint - consider this before naming a beneficial nominee if you need flexibility.

Any  person  OTHER  than  spouse,  child,  or  parent  named  as  nominee  (e.g.,  sibling,  friend,  business  partner)  is  a non-beneficial nominee. They receive the death benefit as a TRUSTEE for the legal heirs of the life assured. In other words, they do not personally own the proceeds - they hold the money on behalf of and must distribute it to the legal heirs.

RECOMMENDATION:  If  you  wish  to  leave  proceeds  to  a  sibling  or  other  relative,  it  is  better  to  name  them  as beneficiary in your Will rather than as a non-beneficial nominee under the policy, to avoid disputes.

- The nominee must be named at the time of policy inception or can be added/changed at any time during the policy term.  -  A  policyholder  can  name  multiple  nominees  and  specify  the  percentage  share  of  the  death  benefit  each nominee will  receive.  -  The  sum  of  all  percentage  shares  must  equal  exactly  100%.  -  If  a  nominee's  share  is  not specified,  equal  shares  are  assumed  among  all  nominees

.  -  A  nominee  does  not  need  to  be  a  blood  relative  (but non-relatives will be non-beneficial nominees). - A nominee cannot be a minor organisation, company, or trust - only natural persons.

If  the nominee is a minor (under 18 years of age), an APPOINTEE must also be named. The appointee is an adult (typically the other parent or a guardian) who will receive and manage the claim proceeds on behalf of the minor until the minor reaches the age of majority (18 years).

REQUIRED INFORMATION FOR MINOR NOMINEE: - Full name of minor nominee - Date of birth of minor nominee Relationship to life assured - Full name, date of birth, and relationship of appointee - Appointee's contact details When the minor nominee turns 18, the appointee's role automatically ceases and the now-adult nominee becomes the direct beneficiary. VitaLife should be notified when the minor turns 18 to update records.

Example 1 - VALID: Spouse 60%, Child 1 (daughter) 20%, Child 2 (son) 20% = 100% 3 Example  2  -  VALID: Parents equally: Father 50%, Mother 50% = 100% 3 Example 3 - INVALID: Wife 60%, Son 60% = 120% 7 (exceeds 100%) Example 4 - INVALID: Wife 40%, Son 40%, Daughter 10% = 90% 7 (does not total 100%)

If invalid shares are submitted, VitaLife will contact the policyholder to correct before processing. Policies issued with unresolved nomination errors may have claims delayed.

Nomination  can  be  changed  at  any  time  during  the  policy  term  by  submitting  Form  NOM-02  (Nomination  Change Request) to any VitaLife branch or online through the policyholder portal.

IMPORTANT: The change of nomination takes effect only from the date VitaLife endorses the change on the policy. A nomination change form submitted but not yet endorsed does NOT override the existing nomination.

EXCEPTION - BENEFICIAL NOMINEE: If you have named a beneficial nominee (spouse, child, parent), you cannot change the nomination without the WRITTEN CONSENT of the current beneficial nominee (or their guardians if minor). This protects beneficial nominees from being unilaterally removed.

If a nominee dies before the life assured and no substitute nominee has been named: The death benefit is payable to the legal heirs of the life assured as per succession laws (not as per the nominee's legal heirs). A succession certificate or probate may be required, causing delays.

metadata.section: What Happens If the Nominee Dies First

text: BEST PRACTICE: Always name substitute nominees or update your nomination if your primary nominee passes away. You can name a second or third nominee as a backup by specifying:  'If  [Primary  Nominee]  predeceases  me,  the benefit shall pass to [Substitute Nominee].'

metadata.section: What Happens If the Nominee Dies First

text: Submit the following to any VitaLife branch or online: - Completed Form NOM-02 (available at vitalife.com/forms) Original  policy  document  (or  request  for  endorsement  on  policy)  -  Nominee's  photo  identity  proof  (Aadhaar,  PAN, passport, voter ID) - Nominee's address proof (if different from policyholder) - For minor nominees: birth certificate of minor; Aadhaar or birth certificate of appointee - For beneficial nominee change: written consent of existing beneficial nominee (Form NOM-03)

text: VitaLife Insurance Corporation | Customer Service | 2025 Edition

A policy lapses when the premium due is not paid within the grace period. The grace period is 30 days for annual, semi-annual, and quarterly premiums, and 15 days for monthly premiums.

CONSEQUENCES OF LAPSE BY PRODUCT TYPE:

TERM LIFE (VitaShield  Term):  Policy  ceases  immediately  after  the  grace  period.  No  death  benefit  is  payable  for deaths occurring after the lapse date. No surrender value or paid-up value exists for term policies. All premiums paid are forfeited.

WHOLE LIFE (VitaGuard) AND ENDOWMENT (VitaSave): If the policy has completed fewer than 3 years of premium payment:  Policy  lapses  with  no  value.  If  the  policy  has  completed  3  or  more  years  of  premium  payment:  Policy automatically converts to a PAID-UP POLICY with a reduced sum assured (paid-up value). Paid-up value = Original sum assured × (Number of premiums paid / Total premiums payable for full term). Bonuses already vested are retained in proportion
. No new bonuses accrue on a paid-up policy.

ULIP  (VitaGrow  Plus):  During  the  5-year  lock-in:  If  premium  is  unpaid  after  the  grace  period,  the  policy  enters  a discontinuance period (2 years). Fund value is moved to the Discontinued Policy Fund (DPF) which earns a minimum of 4% p.a. After the discontinuance period (or after lock-in ends): Policyholder may revive or receive DPF value minus discontinuance charges.

A lapsed policy can be revived within 5 years from the date of the first unpaid premium (or within the policy term, whichever is earlier).

REVIVAL  IS  NOT  POSSIBLE  IF:  The  revival  period  of  5  years  has  expired;  The  life  assured  has  developed  an uninsurable condition (subject to underwriting); The policy was surrendered (surrendered policies cannot be revived).

WHAT REVIVAL REQUIRES: Payment of all outstanding premiums since lapse date, PLUS Interest on outstanding premiums at 9% per annum from due date of each unpaid premium to date of revival payment. A satisfactory health declaration (Form REV-01). For policies lapsed > 2 years: a fresh medical examination (same requirements as new business for age and sum assured). Submission of Form REV-01 (Revival Application) at any VitaLife branch or online.

EXAMPLE: Monthly premium: INR 5,000. Policy lapsed in January 2024 (12 premiums unpaid as of January 2025). Interest rate: 9% p.a.

Total unpaid premiums: 12 × INR 5,000 = INR 60,000 Average period outstanding: ~6.5 months » 0.54 years Interest: INR 60,000 × 9% × 0.54 = INR 2,916 (approximate) Total revival payment: INR 60,000 + INR 2,916 = INR 62,916 (approximate)
Exact interest is calculated on each unpaid premium individually from its due date. Use the VitaLife Revival Calculator at vitalife.com/revival for precise amounts.

VitaLife periodically offers Special Revival Schemes (SRS) that waive or reduce the interest component to encourage policyholders to revive lapsed policies. When an SRS is active: Normal interest charges are reduced or waived. Health requirements may be relaxed for shorter lapse periods. Check vitalife.com/offers or contact your advisor for current SRS offers.
CAUTION: SRS availability varies and is announced with limited validity periods (typically 3-6 months). Do not delay revival in anticipation of an SRS as the lapse period continues to accumulate.

When  a  participating  plan  (Whole  Life  or  Endowment)  lapses  after  3  or  more  years  of  premium  payment,  it automatically becomes a REDUCED PAID-UP (RPU) policy.

PAID-UP SUM ASSURED FORMULA: Paid-Up SA = Original SA × (n / N) where n = number of premiums actually paid, N = total premiums payable for full policy term.

EXAMPLE: 20-year endowment plan, annual premium. SA = INR 10,00,000. Policyholder paid 6 years (6 premiums) then stopped. Paid-Up SA = 10,00,000 × (6/20) = INR 3,00,000. Death benefit: INR 3,00,000 + proportionate vested bonuses.  Maturity  benefit:  INR  3,00,000  +  proportionate  vested  bonuses  (at  end  of  original  20-year  term  -  no extension).

BONUSES ON PAID-UP POLICY: Reversionary bonuses accrued up to the date of lapse are retained in proportion to the paid-up ratio. No new bonuses accrue on a paid-up policy. The paid-up policy continues in force until the end of the original policy term or the life assured's death, whichever is first.

A financial  product  where  the  policyholder  pays  a  lump  sum  or  series  of  payments,  and  in  return  receives  regular income payments, either for life  or  for  a  fixed  period.  VitaLife  offers  immediate  and  deferred  annuity  products  (not covered in this dataset).

The  legal  transfer  of  the  policyholder's  rights  and  interests  in  a  life  insurance  policy  to  another  person  or  entity. Absolute  assignment  transfers  all  rights  permanently;  conditional  assignment  transfers  rights  subject  to  specified conditions.

A nominee who is a spouse, child, or parent of the life assured. A beneficial nominee has an absolute right to the policy proceeds on the life assured's death and is protected from claims by creditors and other legal heirs.

An addition to the sum assured, declared annually by the insurer as a percentage of the sum assured, for participating (with-profits) policies. Once declared, it cannot be taken away. It is paid along with the sum assured at maturity or death.
A one-time bonus declared by VitaLife at the time of policy termination (death, maturity, or surrender) in addition to reversionary bonuses. Not guaranteed; depends on fund performance.

The  amount  paid  to  the  nominee(s)  upon  the  death  of  the  life  assured  during  the  policy  term.  For  term  life:  sum assured. For participating plans: sum assured plus accrued bonuses. For ULIP: higher of fund value or sum assured.

A period of 15 days (30 days for policies sold online or by direct marketing) from the date of receipt of the policy document, during which the policyholder may return the policy for a full refund of premium, minus proportionate risk premium and medical costs.
The current market value of units held in a ULIP policy, calculated by multiplying the number of units by the current Net Asset Value (NAV) of the fund.
A period after the premium due date during which the policy remains in force without lapse. VitaLife grace period: 30 days for annual/semi-annual/quarterly premiums; 15 days for monthly premiums.

The  minimum  surrender  value  guaranteed  by  the  policy.  GSV  =  30%  of  total  premiums  paid  (excluding  first-year premium and rider premiums) after the policy has been in force for 3 years. GSV increases over time.
Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India - the statutory body regulating the insurance industry in India. VitaLife is licensed and regulated by IRDAI.

The termination of a policy due to non-payment of premium after the grace period. A lapsed term policy has no value; a lapsed participating plan converts to paid-up (if 3+ years premiums paid) or lapses without value.
The benefit paid to the policyholder (life assured) when the policy term ends and the life assured is alive. Applicable to endowment and whole life plans and ULIP. Term life has no maturity benefit.
VitaLife Insurance Corporation | Reference Document | 2025
A monthly deduction in ULIP to provide the life insurance coverage. Calculated based on the 'sum at risk' (sum assured minus fund value) and the life assured's age. Increases with age.

The per-unit value of a ULIP fund, calculated daily as (Total fund assets minus liabilities) / Number of units outstanding. ULIP premiums are allocated as units at the prevailing NAV on the date of allocation.
The process by which the policyholder designates a person (nominee) to receive the death benefit if the life assured dies during the policy term.

A policy that has been in force for at least 3 years (for participating plans) and for which no further premiums will be paid, but which continues in force for a reduced sum assured (paid-up value) until the end of the original policy term.

A loan taken against the surrender value of a life insurance policy. VitaLife allows loans of up to 85% of surrender value for participating plans and 40% of fund value for ULIPs. Outstanding loan plus interest is deducted from the claim or maturity amount.

An  additional  premium  charged  over  the  standard  tabular  rate  for  applicants  assessed  as  substandard  health  or occupational risks. Expressed as a percentage of the standard premium (e.g., +25%, +50%).

The reinstatement of a lapsed policy by paying all outstanding premiums with interest and submitting a satisfactory health declaration. Revival must occur within 5 years of the first unpaid premium date.
An optional add-on benefit attached to a base life insurance policy for additional coverage. Common riders: Critical Illness, Accidental Death Benefit, Waiver of Premium, Permanent Total Disability.
A section of the Indian Income Tax Act allowing deduction of life insurance premiums paid from taxable income, up to INR 1,50,000 per year.

A section of the Indian Income Tax Act exempting death and maturity proceeds of life insurance policies from income tax, subject to conditions (premium must be £ 10% of sum assured for policies issued after April 1, 2012).
Not  applicable  in  life  insurance  (applicable  in  general  insurance).  Life  insurance  death  benefits  are  not  subject  to subrogation.
The guaranteed amount payable as the death benefit (and, for endowment/whole life, the maturity benefit). Chosen by the policyholder at inception.

The amount payable when a policyholder voluntarily terminates the policy before its maturity. Equal to the higher of the Guaranteed Surrender Value (GSV) or Special Surrender Value (SSV). Surrendering early typically results in a loss relative to premiums paid.

A life insurance product combining insurance protection with market-linked investment. Premiums are split between risk cover (mortality charge) and investment in market funds of the policyholder's choice.

The process by which VitaLife assesses the risk of insuring an applicant, based on health, age, occupation, lifestyle, and financial profile, to determine eligibility and premium rate.

VitaLife  offers  four  core  life  insurance  products  designed  to  meet  different  financial  goals,  life  stages,  and  risk appetites. This guide provides a comprehensive comparison of each product, their features, suitability criteria, and key terms.

Maximum Protection. Minimum Premium.

VitaShield Term Life is a pure protection plan that provides a high sum assured at an affordable premium. If the life assured dies during the policy term, the full sum assured is paid to the nominee. There is no maturity benefit - if the life assured survives the policy term, no amount is payable. This makes term life the most cost-effective way to provide income replacement and financial security for dependents.

COVERAGE AMOUNTS: Minimum sum assured: INR  25,00,000  (25  lakhs).  Maximum:  No  upper  limit  (subject  to underwriting).

POLICY TERMS: 10, 15, 20, 25, or 30 years. Entry age: 18-65 years. Maximum maturity age: 75 years.

PREMIUM  PAYMENT:  Level  premium  (same  throughout  the  policy  term).  Single  pay  option  available.  Annual, semi-annual,  quarterly,  or  monthly  payment  frequency.  Grace  period:  30  days  for  annual/semi-annual/quarterly;  15 days for monthly.

PREMIUM FACTORS: Age, gender, sum assured, policy term, smoking status, occupation, medical history, and BMI. Women receive a 5% premium discount. Non-smokers receive a 7.5% premium discount.

DEATH BENEFIT: 100% of sum assured paid to nominee as lump sum. Option to receive benefit as monthly income (10 years) instead of lump sum. Return of Premium (ROP) variant available: full premiums returned at end of term (at higher premium).

RIDERS  AVAILABLE:  Critical  Illness  Rider  (CI):  Additional  sum  assured  if  diagnosed  with  listed  critical  illness. Accidental Death Benefit Rider (ADB): Additional sum assured if death is accidental. Waiver of Premium Rider (WOP): Future premiums waived if policyholder becomes permanently disabled. Permanent Total Disability Rider (PTD): Sum assured paid if policyholder suffers PTD.

BEST SUITED FOR: Young earners with dependents who need maximum coverage at minimum cost; Home loan or business loan borrowers who want loan coverage; Primary breadwinners with limited insurance budget; Those who have other investment vehicles (PPF, mutual funds) for savings.

NOT SUITABLE FOR: Those seeking a savings or investment component; Those wanting a guaranteed return or maturity payout; Senior applicants (over 60) where premium costs escalate significantly; Those wanting a plan to leave behind wealth (consider Whole Life instead).
Protection for Life. Savings for Legacy.

VitaGuard Whole Life is a participating (with-profits) life insurance plan providing coverage for the whole of life (up to age 99) combined with a cash value accumulation feature. The plan pays a death benefit to nominees whenever the life  assured  dies  -  there  is  no  expiry  of  coverage.  The  plan  also  accumulates  cash  value  through  reversionary bonuses declared annually by VitaLife.

COVERAGE AMOUNTS: Minimum sum assured: INR 5,00,000. Maximum: Subject to underwriting. Entry age: 0 (28 days) to 60 years. Coverage continues to age 99.

PREMIUM PAYMENT OPTIONS: Regular pay: Premiums paid for the entire policy term. Limited pay: Premiums paid for 10, 15, or 20 years; coverage continues for life. Single pay: One-time premium. Note: Limited pay and single pay have higher per-instalment premiums.

CASH  VALUE  &  SURRENDER  VALUE:  Cash  value  begins  accumulating  after  policy  year  3.  Surrender  value  = Guaranteed Surrender Value (GSV) or Special Surrender Value (SSV), whichever is higher. GSV: 30% of premiums paid (excluding first year and rider premiums) after 3 years; increases to 50% after year 7 and 90% after year 10. Policy loan available: up to 85% of surrender value.

BONUSES: Reversionary Bonus: Declared annually as a percentage of sum assured; once added, cannot be taken away.  Terminal  Bonus:  Paid  at  maturity,  death,  or  surrender  (at  VitaLife's  discretion  based  on  fund  performance). Current indicative reversionary bonus: 4.2% per annum of sum assured (not guaranteed; based on 2024 performance).

MATURITY BENEFIT: If  the  life  assured  survives  to  age  99:  Sum  Assured  +  all  accrued  reversionary  bonuses  + terminal bonus is paid.

BEST  SUITED  FOR:  Individuals  seeking  lifelong  coverage  with  no  risk  of  outliving  the  policy;  Estate  planning  leaving a legacy for heirs; Those who want forced savings alongside protection; Business partners needing key person or buy-sell agreement coverage; Parents seeking coverage that can be transferred to children.

NOT SUITABLE FOR: Those seeking high  investment  returns  (ULIP  or  mutual  funds  outperform);  Young  earners needing maximum coverage at minimum cost (term life is better); Those with a short investment horizon (surrender value in early years is low).
Save. Protect. Achieve Your Goals.

VitaSave  Endowment  is  a  participating  savings-cum-protection  plan.  It  combines  life  insurance  coverage  with  a guaranteed savings goal: the policy pays the sum assured plus accumulated bonuses either on death (to nominees) or on  survival  to  the  end  of  the  policy  term  (to  the  policyholder).  This  dual-purpose  structure  makes  it  suitable  for goal-based saving - children's education, marriage, home purchase, or retirement.

COVERAGE AMOUNTS: Minimum sum assured: INR 1,00,000. Maximum: No upper limit (subject to underwriting). Entry age: 0 (91 days) to 60 years. Maturity age: Maximum 70 years.

POLICY TERMS: 10, 15, 20, or 25 years (fixed term - not whole of life). Premium payment: Level throughout the term. Single pay option available for 10-year plans.

MATURITY BENEFIT (Survival Benefit): If the life assured survives to the end of the policy term: Sum Assured + all accrued  reversionary  bonuses  +  terminal  bonus  is  paid.  This  is  the  policyholder's  savings  goal  payout.  Current indicative maturity bonus: 4.0% per annum reversionary bonus (not guaranteed).

DEATH BENEFIT: Sum assured + all accrued bonuses paid to nominee. In the early years of the policy, total death benefit may be higher than surrender value.

SURRENDER VALUE: Available  from  year  3  onwards.  Similar  GSV/SSV  structure  as  Whole  Life.  Surrendering  a participating endowment plan early forfeits a significant portion of accumulated bonuses.

LOAN FACILITY: Policy loan available after year 3: up to 85% of surrender value at prevailing VitaLife lending rate (currently 9.5% p.a. simple interest).

BEST SUITED FOR: Goal-based  savers  with  a  defined  financial  target  and  timeline  (e.g.,  child's  education  in  15 years); Conservative investors who prefer guaranteed returns with protection; Those who want a disciplined savings vehicle with a safety net; Applicants who are not eligible for high-return instruments due to risk aversion.

NOT  SUITABLE  FOR:  Those  seeking  flexible  premium  or  investment  options  (ULIP  is  better);  High  net-worth individuals with sophisticated investment portfolios (returns may lag); Those with a need for high pure coverage at low cost (term life provides more coverage per rupee).
Grow Your Wealth. Protect Your Future.

VitaGrow  Plus  is  a  Unit-Linked  Insurance  Plan  (ULIP)  that  combines  life  insurance  protection  with  market-linked investment. A portion of the premium goes towards life cover; the remainder is invested in funds of the policyholder's choice (equity, debt, or balanced). The death benefit is the higher of the fund value or the sum assured, providing a safety net regardless of market performance.

COVERAGE  AMOUNTS:  Minimum  sum  assured:  10x  annualised  premium.  Maximum:  40x  annualised  premium (higher  subject  to  underwriting  and  age).  Entry  age:  0  (91  days)  to  65  years.  Maximum  maturity  age:  75  years. Minimum policy term: 10 years. Lock-in: 5 years (IRDAI-mandated; no withdrawals before year 5).

FUND  OPTIONS:  VitaGrow  Equity  Fund:  80-100%  equity;  high  risk/high  return;  benchmark:  Nifty  50.  VitaGrow Balanced Fund: 40-60% equity, remainder in debt; moderate risk. VitaGrow Debt Fund: 0-20% equity, 80-100% debt instruments; low risk. VitaGrow Liquid Fund: 100% money market instruments; capital preservation. VitaGrow Dynamic Fund: Actively managed asset allocation; fund manager discretion.

CHARGES: Premium Allocation Charge (PAC): Year 1: 5%, Year 2: 4%, Year 3+: 2%. Policy Administration Charge (PAC):  Rs.  60/month  (Year  1-5);  Rs.  40/month  (Year  6+).  Fund  Management  Charge  (FMC):  Equity:  1.35%  p.a.; Balanced: 1.10% p.a.; Debt/Liquid: 0.75% p.a. Mortality Charge (MC): Deducted monthly from fund value based on age and sum at risk. Surrender Charge (SC): Year 1-5: Not applicable (locked in); Year 6: 2%; Year 7: 1%; Year 8+: Nil.

PARTIAL WITHDRAWALS: Allowed after the 5-year lock-in. Minimum withdrawal: Rs. 5,000. Maximum: Up to 20% of fund value per year. Fund value must remain above 105% of sum assured after withdrawal.

SWITCHING BETWEEN FUNDS: 4 free switches per policy year. Additional switches: Rs. 250 per switch.

DEATH BENEFIT: Higher of (a) fund value at time of death, or (b) sum assured minus all partial withdrawals in last 2 years. Death claim settled within 30 days of submission of all documents.

BEST SUITED FOR: Long-term investors (10+ year horizon) who want market-linked growth; Individuals comfortable with equity market volatility; Those who want flexibility to change investment allocation; Investors who want insurance and investment in one product for simplicity; Young professionals in the accumulation phase of wealth.

NOT SUITABLE FOR: Risk-averse individuals seeking guaranteed returns; Short-term investors (the 5-year lock-in and  high  early  charges  make  short-term  exits  expensive);  Those  with  purely  protection  needs  (term  life  is  more cost-effective for coverage); Senior applicants (high mortality charges reduce investment corpus).

VitaLife Insurance Corporation | Master Policy Document | 2025

DEATH BENEFIT: The amount payable to the nominee upon the death of the life assured during the policy term.

FREE LOOK PERIOD: A period of 15 days (30 days for policies sold through distance marketing) from the date of receipt of the policy document during which the policyholder may return the policy and receive a refund of premium paid, minus proportionate risk premium and medical examination expenses.

GRACE PERIOD: A period after the premium due date during which the policy remains in force. Grace period: 30 days for  premiums payable annually, semi-annually, or quarterly; 15 days for monthly premiums. Death during the grace period: claim is payable after deduction of outstanding premium.

LAPSE: A policy that has not been revived after the grace period expires. A lapsed policy has no cash value (for term life) or reduced paid-up value (for participating plans) until revived.

LIFE ASSURED: The person whose life is insured under the policy. May be the same as the policyholder or a different person.

MATURITY DATE: The date on  which  the  policy  term  ends  and  the  maturity  benefit  (where  applicable)  becomes payable.

NOMINEE:  The  person(s)  designated  by  the  policyholder  to  receive  the  death  benefit  upon  the  death  of  the  life assured.

PAID-UP POLICY: A policy where the policyholder has stopped paying premiums but the policy remains in force for a reduced sum assured (paid-up value). Applicable to participating plans after at least 3 years of premium payment.

POLICYHOLDER: The person who owns the policy and is responsible for paying premiums.

REVIVAL: The process of reinstating a lapsed policy. Revival is allowed within 5 years of the first unpaid premium date, subject to satisfactory health declaration and payment of all outstanding premiums with interest.

RIDER: An optional add-on benefit that enhances the base policy coverage. Rider premiums are payable in addition to the base policy premium.

SUM ASSURED (SUM AT RISK): The guaranteed amount payable as the death benefit or maturity benefit as specified in the policy schedule.

SURRENDER VALUE: The amount payable to the policyholder  upon  early  termination  of  the  policy.  Equal  to  the higher of Guaranteed Surrender Value (GSV) or Special Surrender Value (SSV). Applicable only to participating plans (Whole Life and Endowment) and ULIP.

PROPOSAL FORM: The policyholder must complete VitaLife's standard proposal form truthfully and completely. Any material misrepresentation, non-disclosure, or fraud in the proposal form may result in the policy being declared void.

MEDICAL EXAMINATION: Required based on age,  sum  assured,  and  health  history.  VitaLife  may  waive  medical examination for younger applicants with lower sum assured and clean health history.

UNDERWRITING DECISION: Based on the proposal, medical reports, and risk assessment. Possible outcomes: (a) Standard  rates  -  no  extra  premium  loading;  (b)  Substandard  rates  -  extra  premium  loading  due  to  health, occupational,  or  lifestyle  risk  factors;  (c)  Postponement  -  application  deferred  pending  additional  information;  (d) Decline - application rejected due to unacceptable risk.

POLICY DOCUMENT DELIVERY: Policy document will be delivered within 15 days of acceptance of proposal and receipt of first premium. The policyholder should review all details and inform VitaLife of any discrepancies within 30 days.

After the policy has been in force for 3 consecutive years from the date of commencement (or revival), VitaLife shall not contest  the  validity  of  the  policy  on  the  grounds  of  misrepresentation  or  non-disclosure  of  material  facts,  except  in cases of fraud.

FRAUD EXCEPTION: VitaLife may contest a policy at any time on the grounds of proven fraudulent misrepresentation, even after 3 years.

PAYMENT METHODS: Premium may be paid via NACH (auto-debit), online banking, UPI, cheque, or demand draft payable to VitaLife Insurance Corporation.

PREMIUM RECEIPT: A premium  receipt  will  be  issued  for  every  premium  payment.  Premium  payment  history  is available on the VitaLife policyholder portal at vitalife.com/myaccount.

REINSTATEMENT AFTER GRACE PERIOD LAPSE: If the premium is not paid within the grace period, the policy lapses. For participating plans (Whole Life, Endowment): the policy may convert to a reduced paid-up policy (if 3+ years of premiums paid) or lapse without value. For term life: no survival benefit; policy lapses with no value.

Applicants  assessed  as  substandard  risks  will  be  charged  an  extra  premium  over  the  standard  tabular  rate.  Extra premium  loading  categories:  Class  I  (Low  Risk):  +25%  of  standard  premium  Class  II  (Moderate  Risk):  +50%  of standard premium Class III (High Risk): +100% of standard premium Class IV (Very High Risk): +150% of standard premium or postponement/decline

Examples of conditions attracting extra premium loading: - Controlled hypertension (well-managed): Class I - Type 2 diabetes  (well-controlled,  HbA1c  <  8%):  Class  II  -  Obesity  (BMI  35-39.9):  Class  I-II  depending  on  other  factors  History  of  cancer  (5+  years  in  remission):  Class  II-III  depending  on  type  -  High-risk  occupation  (mining,  oil  &  gas, armed forces): Class I-II
The following exclusions apply to all VitaLife policies. Death resulting from these causes will NOT be covered:

- (a) SUICIDE: Death by suicide within 12 months of policy commencement or revival. (Note: After 12 months, suicide is covered in accordance with IRDAI regulations.)
- (b)  HAZARDOUS  ACTIVITIES:  Death  while  participating  in  aviation  other  than  as  a  fare-paying  passenger  on  a licensed commercial airline; motor racing; mountaineering above 6,000 metres; skydiving; bungee jumping; deep-sea diving.

- (c) SELF-INFLICTED INJURY: Death resulting from intentional self-harm (not meeting suicide definition).
- (d) CRIMINAL ACTS: Death while committing or attempting to commit a cognisable criminal offence.
- (e) WAR AND CIVIL UNREST: Death directly caused by war (declared or undeclared), invasion, rebellion, or military action.
- (f) NUCLEAR HAZARD: Death caused by nuclear fission, fusion, contamination, or radioactive fallout.

- (g)  INTOXICATION:  Death  where  blood  alcohol  level  exceeds  legal  limits  or  where  the  deceased  was  under  the influence of illegal drugs at the time of death.
- (h)  HIV/AIDS:  Death  resulting  directly  from  HIV/AIDS  (applies  only  to  policies  issued  before  April  1,  2020;  policies issued after this date cover HIV/AIDS in accordance with IRDAI circular LI/MISC/142).

NOTE ON WAITING PERIODS: Certain critical illness riders have a 90-day waiting period from policy inception; CI claims during this period are not payable.

NOTE  ON  ACCIDENTAL  DEATH  BENEFIT  RIDER:  The  ADB  rider  exclusions  additionally  include  death  due  to self-administered substances (including overdose of prescription medication), death while insane, and death due to bacterial infection (unless resulting from an accidental cut or wound).

STEP 1 - INTIMATION: Notify VitaLife Claims Department as soon as possible after the death of the life assured. Intimation  can  be  given  at  any  VitaLife  branch,  online  at  vitalife.com/claims,  or  by  calling  1-800-VL-CLAIM (1-800-855-2524).

STEP 2 - CLAIM FORM: Download and complete the Death Claim Form (DCF-01) from vitalife.com/claims. The form must be signed by the nominee(s).

STEP  3  -  DOCUMENTATION:  Submit  the  following  documents:  Mandatory:  Original  policy  document;  Death certificate  (certified  copy  from  local  authority);  Death  claim  form  (DCF-01);  Nominee's  photo  ID  and  address  proof; Nominee's  bank  account  details  (cancelled  cheque  or  bank  passbook  copy).  Additional  for  non-natural  deaths: Post-mortem report; Police FIR (if applicable); Panchnama; Medical examiner's certificate
. Additional for accidental death claims: Police FIR; Motor accident report (if vehicle accident); Newspaper clipping (if major accident).

STEP 4 - INVESTIGATION: VitaLife may appoint a claim investigator for claims within 3 years of policy issuance, claims above INR 50,00,000, or claims where cause of death is unclear.

STEP 5 - SETTLEMENT: Once all documents are received and verified: Early death claims (within 3 years): Settled within 30 days of receipt of all documents. All other claims: Settled within 30 days.
STEP 6 - PAYMENT: Death benefit paid directly to nominee's bank account via NEFT/RTGS. If the nominee is a minor, payment is made to the appointee named in the policy.

Maturity claims (Endowment, Whole Life, ULIP) are processed automatically by VitaLife: 30 days before maturity date: VitaLife  sends  a  Maturity  Intimation  Letter  to  the  registered  address.  15  days  before  maturity  date:  Policyholder submits: Original policy document; Maturity claim discharge form; Bank account details. On maturity date: Payment credited to policyholder's bank account by NEFT/RTGS.

ELIGIBILITY: Policy must have acquired a surrender value (typically after 3 years of premium payment for participating plans; after 5 years for ULIP).

MAXIMUM LOAN AMOUNT: Whole Life / Endowment: Up to 85% of surrender value ULIP: Up to 40% of fund value

INTEREST  RATE:  Prevailing  VitaLife  policy  loan  rate,  currently  9.5%  per  annum,  compounded  annually.  Interest accrues from the date of loan disbursement.

REPAYMENT: No fixed repayment schedule. Outstanding loan + accrued interest will be deducted from the claim amount (death benefit, maturity benefit, or surrender value) if not repaid.

FORECLOSURE: If outstanding loan + interest equals or exceeds the surrender value at any time, VitaLife will send a 30-day  notice.  If  not  repaid  within  30  days,  the  policy  will  be  foreclosed  (terminated)  and  any  residual  amount (surrender value minus loan) will be paid.

A  nominee  is  entitled  to  receive  the  death  benefit  if  the  life  assured  dies  during  the  policy  term.  BENEFICIAL NOMINEE (Section  39  of  Insurance  Act  1938):  Spouse,  children,  and  parents  named  as  nominees  are  beneficial nominees and have an absolute right to the policy proceeds. No other claimant (including creditors) can claim the proceeds
. OTHER NOMINEES: Any other person may be named as nominee; however, they receive proceeds as trustees for the legal heirs of the life assured.

NOMINATION OF MINOR: If nominee is a minor, an appointee (an adult) must be named. The appointee holds the proceeds in trust for the minor until majority.

CHANGE  OF  NOMINATION:  The  policyholder  may  change  the  nominee  at  any  time  during  the  policy  term  by submitting a Nomination Change Request (Form NOM-02) to any VitaLife branch or online.

MULTIPLE NOMINEES: Multiple nominees may be named with specified percentage shares. Shares must total 100%. If a nominee predeceases the life assured, their share passes equally to surviving nominees.

The policyholder may assign the policy to another person or entity (e.g., as collateral for a bank loan). Assignment must be in writing on VitaLife's Assignment Form (Form ASN-01) and submitted for endorsement. Types: Absolute Assignment  -  transfers  all  rights  to  the  assignee  permanently;  Conditional  Assignment  -  transfers  rights  under specific conditions (e.g., lender recovers outstanding loan; remaining benefit goes back to nominee).

A policy with a registered assignment cannot be surrendered or modified without the assignee's consent.

This  manual  provides  the  underwriting  criteria  and  risk  classification  guidelines  used  by  VitaLife  to  assess  life insurance  applications.  Participants  should  use  this  document  to  simulate  underwriting  risk  assessment  in  the  AI copilot.

| Age Band   | Sum Assured (INR)   | Medical Requirements                                                       |
|------------|---------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 18-35      | Up to 50 lakhs      | No medical (self-declaration only)                                         |
| 18-35      | 50 lakhs - 1 crore  | Basic medical: CBC, lipid profile, urine routine, HIV, BP                  |

| 18-35      | Above 1 crore       | Full medical: CBC, lipid, urine, HIV, BP, blood sugar, ECG, liver function |
| 36-45      | Up to 25 lakhs      | No medical (self-declaration only)                                         |
| 36-45      | 25 lakhs - 75 lakhs | Basic medical + stress test (treadmill)                                    |
| 36-45      | Above 75 lakhs      | Full medical + stress test + 2D Echo + chest X-ray                         |

| 46-55      | Up to 10 lakhs      | Basic medical                                                              |
| 46-55      | 10 lakhs - 50 lakhs | Full medical + stress test + 2D Echo + chest X-ray                         |
| 46-55      | Above 50 lakhs      | Full medical + stress test + 2D Echo + specialist opinion                  |
| 56-65      | All amounts         | Full medical + stress test + 2D Echo + chest X-ray + renal function        |

The  following  table  shows  common  medical  conditions  and  their  standard  underwriting  classification  at  VitaLife. Classification may change based on severity, control, duration, and combination with other risk factors.

| No significant history                         | Standard                   | Nil                     | Age-appropriate medical only                                 | Best class; lowest premium                                               |
| Well-controlled hypertension (BP £ 140/90)     | Standard - Class I         | Nil - +25%              | BP readings for last 6 months; treating physician report     | Loading depends on duration and other CV risk factors                    |

| Poorly controlled hypertension (BP > 160/100)  | Substandard - Class II     | +50%                    | Cardiologist report; ECG; 2D Echo                            | Consider decline if BP > 180/110 or end-organ damage                     |
| Type 2 Diabetes (HbA1c £ 8%, no complications) | Substandard - Class I-II   | +25% to +50%            | HbA1c; fasting glucose; creatinine; urine microalbumin       | Loading based on duration, control, and complications                    |

| Type 2 Diabetes (HbA1c > 9%, or complications) | Substandard - Class III    | +75% to +100%           | Full metabolic panel; ophthalmologist report; renal function | Decline if HbA1c > 11% or advanced nephropathy/neuropathy                |
| Type 1 Diabetes                                | Substandard - Class III-IV | +100% to +150%          | Endocrinologist report; HbA1c; full organ function           | Typically Class III or IV; early-onset juvenile diabetes: higher loading |

| BMI 25-29.9 (Overweight)                       | Standard                   | Nil                     | None additional                                              | No loading if no other risk factors                                      |

| BMI 30-34.9 (Obese)                             | Standard - Class I         | Nil - +25%              | BP, blood sugar, lipid profile                                     | Loading if other metabolic risk factors present                      |
| BMI 35-39.9 (Severely Obese)                    | Substandard - Class I-II   | +25% to +50%            | Cardiologist or physician evaluation                               | Decline if BMI > 45 or severely obese with multiple comorbidities    |

| BMI ‡ 40 (Morbidly Obese)                       | Substandard - Class II-III | +50% to +75%            | Full cardiac and metabolic evaluation                              | Consider postponement if recent bariatric surgery                    |
| Smoking (current, < 10 cigarettes/day)          | Smoker rates apply         | +30-40% over standard   | Urine cotinine test                                                | Smoker tables used; cessation > 12 months = non-smoker rates         |

| Smoking (current, ‡ 10 cigarettes/day)          | Smoker rates apply         | +50-60% over standard   | Urine cotinine test; chest X-ray                                   | Heavy smoking with age > 45: additional loading                      |
| Asthma (mild, well-controlled)                  | Standard                   | Nil                     | Pulmonologist certificate if recent hospitalisation                | No loading if no hospitalisation in 2 years and good lung function   |

| Asthma (moderate to severe)                     | Substandard - Class I      | +25%                    | PFT (spirometry); recent treatment history                         | Decline if on systemic steroids currently                            |
| Cancer - in remission < 5 years                 | Postpone or Class III-IV   | +75% to +150%           | Oncologist report; pathology; current surveillance scans           | Depends on cancer type and stage; some cancers: decline              |

| Cancer - in remission ‡ 5 years                 | Substandard - Class II-III | +50% to +75%            | Oncologist clearance letter; recent surveillance                   | Skin cancer (basal cell): standard rates possible                    |
| History of heart attack (MI) - > 5 years ago    | Substandard - Class II-III | +50% to +100%           | Cardiologist report; ECG; 2D Echo; stress test; recent angiography | Depends on EF, current medications, subsequent events                |

| History of stroke (CVA) - > 3 years ago         | Substandard - Class III    | +75% to +100%           | Neurologist report; MRI brain; functional assessment               | Decline if residual neurological deficit is significant              |
| Kidney disease (CKD Stage 1-2)                  | Substandard - Class I      | +25%                    | Renal function tests; urine microalbumin; nephrologist report      | Monitor creatinine progression                                       |

| Kidney disease (CKD Stage 3+)                   | Decline or Class IV        | +150% or decline        | Nephrologist report; dialysis status                               | CKD Stage 5 (dialysis): decline                                      |
| HIV positive (on ART, undetectable viral load)  | Substandard - Class II-III | +50% to +75%            | Infectious disease specialist report; CD4 count; viral load        | Per IRDAI circular LI/MISC/142; policies issued from April 2020      |

| Liver disease (cirrhosis, active hepatitis B/C) | Postpone or Decline        | N/A                     | Hepatologist report; LFT; viral load                               | Compensated cirrhosis: Class IV; decompensated: decline              |
| Mental health (mild anxiety/depression, stable) | Standard - Class I         | Nil - +25%              | Treating psychiatrist/psychologist report                          | Stability, medication compliance, and no hospitalisation key factors |

| Mental health (hospitalisation in last 2 years) | Substandard - Class III    | +75%                    | Psychiatrist report; discharge summary                             | Decline if active psychosis or high suicide risk                     |
| Occupation - desk/office work                   | Standard                   | Nil                     | None                                                               | Lowest occupational risk class                                       |

| Occupation - skilled manual (driver, electrician) | Class I                | +25%                    | Occupation declaration form                              | Moderate occupational loading             |
| Occupation - mining / oil & gas / armed forces    | Class II-III           | +50% to +75%            | Employer certificate; occupational risk declaration      | Armed forces: war exclusion endorsement   |

| Occupation - pilot (commercial)                   | Substandard - Class II | +50%                    | DGCA medical certificate; flying hours; type of aircraft | Helicopter and aerobatics: higher loading |

| Class A (Standard)       | Low-risk, sedentary or light work                             | Accountant, teacher, doctor, software engineer, banker, manager, clerk                                                    | Nil                      |
| Class B (Low Risk)       | Moderate physical activity; low injury risk                   | Nurse, pharmacist, salesperson, photographer, real estate agent, technician (indoor)                                      | Nil - +10%               |

| Class C (Medium Risk)    | Regular exposure to physical risk or hazardous environment    | Driver (light commercial), electrician, plumber, construction supervisor, farmer, fireman (administrative)                | +25% to +50%             |
| Class D (High Risk)      | Significant physical danger; injury or fatality risk elevated | Mining worker, oil & gas worker, soldier/sailor/airforce (non-combat), fisherman, logging worker, structural steel worker | +50% to +75%             |

| Class E (Very High Risk) | Extreme physical danger; regular life risk exposure           | Combat military, active bomb disposal, test pilot, offshore oil rig worker, deep-sea diver                                | +75% to +150% or Decline |
